extracted.intended_audience: authors, publishers, and others interested in submitting or learning about the National Book Awards
extracted.subtask_description: Overview page for the National Book Awards describing the program, categories, judges, and related submission/eligibility resources for books published in the award year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award categories honored
rubrics_metrics.description: The Awards currently honor the best Fiction, Nonfiction, Poetry, Translated Literature, and Young People’s Literature, published each year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These five categories define the genres eligible for consideration; submissions and judging are organized around these categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mission standard — 'best writing in America'
rubrics_metrics.description: The National Book Awards were established in 1950 to celebrate the best writing in America.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Foundation's mission — to celebrate the best of American literature, expand its audience, and enhance the cultural value of great writing — frames the awards' evaluative orientation (i.e., recognition of outstanding literary quality and cultural value).

rubrics_metrics.name: Judging composition and selection process
rubrics_metrics.description: Twenty-five judges in five categories will review submitted titles and select the five Winners of the 75th National Book Awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection is made by panels of judges (peer reviewers) assigned by category; judges review submitted titles and choose winners and presumably longlists/finalists per category.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility and submissions process (linked)
rubrics_metrics.description: 2024 Submissions — Eligibility, the submissions process, current prizes, guidelines, FAQ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed eligibility criteria, submission procedures, prize information, and FAQs are provided on the linked submissions/guidelines page and govern which titles can be entered and how; this landing page references but does not reproduce those rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medallions and image/seal rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Seals and digital image rights are available for NBA Winner, Finalist, and Longlist titles. In addition to medallions for individual titles, we also offer medallions for 5 Under 35 honorees and Distinguished Contribution to American Letters medalists, which can be used for future or backlist titles, respectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awarded titles (winners, finalists, longlist, and certain honorees) receive official marks and usage rights; this is a production/marketing consideration for publishers of awarded books.
